feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/communications CV with credible scope, clear public-sector positioning, and solid evidence of progression. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is too dense, somewhat repetitive, and would be stronger with sharper outcomes and tighter structure.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director, culminating in enterprise-scale ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility signals: specific platforms, tools, scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), and recent project examples support expertise.  
- Writing is polished and consistent overall, with strong action verbs and a coherent niche in digital platform modernization for mission-driven organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; several themes/tools appear multiple times. Consolidating would improve scannability.  
- Add more impact/results beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, production savings, workflow efficiency gains, adoption rates, or campaign outcomes.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s” style varies; “French (A2/Learning)” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning)”; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization may look inconsistent unless intentional. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It reads well, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it would benefit from sharper positioning and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one concise value proposition plus one scope sentence; avoid listing too many capability areas already covered elsewhere.
- Add 1–2 concrete scale markers from recent roles, e.g. “10,000+ page web estate,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger, more executive phrasing such as “leading modernization of” or “shaping.”
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web platforms, governance, and content operations. Led enterprise website transformation for a 10,000+ page Drupal ecosystem serving 3.5M annual page views, while strengthening analytics, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid restating broad capability lists in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating broad areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure.
- Emphasize highest-value, recent strengths: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia operations.
- Replace “Advocacy and public-sector communications” with a more distinctive capability tied to platform/content leadership.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel content and campaign operations • Public-sector digital communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” already appear in the header.
- This section overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; consider using it only for broad differentiators, not tool- or function-level detail.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes, scope, or distinct formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [thing] using [methods/features] to [outcome].”
- Tighten wording: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for future campaign expansion”; spell out “10 × 20-foot” consistently.
- Consider this rewrite: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search—Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery. We Are Counties Microsite—Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and reusable modules for future expansion. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Created a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 × 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Launched a recurring advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and Advocacy Video Series substantially overlap with current freelance/NACo experience bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs if keeping this section.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance to your headline, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the footer project summaries and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around scope, technical leadership, and outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets and lead with impact: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet more outcome-focused: mention number of sites, users, launches, or efficiency gains if available; e.g., “Developed Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsites, and member toolkits that accelerated campaign launches.”
- Keep AI search, but specify result if possible: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and Drupal microsite work duplicate the “Recent Projects” section; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold examples.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language also overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize what is new in this consulting engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles. Lead with enterprise transformation, then select 3–4 signature wins.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, video production, and multi-channel operations.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more measurable where possible: add budget/team size, reporting improvements, production volume, engagement growth, cost savings, or turnaround gains.
- Combine lower-value bullets: merge email/social oversight with governance/planning into one concise operations bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Video studio language may overlap with older video-production bullets; emphasize building institutional capacity, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like responsibilities than achievements. Tighten it to emphasize what changed under your leadership and how this role set up the later director-level work.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + impact: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Launched/expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable or directional outcomes if available: newsletter growth, open/click rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved workflows” and “strengthened editorial planning” overlap with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version focused on execution/scale, not governance.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the earlier Digital Media Manager role; distinguish this as expansion/operationalization rather than initial creation.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list rather than a senior, applied capability set. It also overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” so this item should emphasize implementation depth and modernize the phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Front-End & Technical Implementation** to better signal applied delivery.
- Rewrite as: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, replace older/generic terms with stronger, outcome-linked phrasing: **Front-end development (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript), third-party/API integrations, tag management (GTM), edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers), CI/CD automation (GitHub Actions)**
- Consider dropping **jQuery** or moving it to the end unless it is still actively used in recent work; prioritize current tools tied to recent Drupal/CMS delivery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution** (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”).
- **Workflow automation** appears elsewhere; avoid implying GitHub Actions duplicates broader automation tools in the next item.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around orchestration/operations tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools**

- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack and Teams are collaboration tools, not workflow systems; grouping prevents the title from feeling overstated.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused without repeating channel-management claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one capability layer instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, segmentation**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, order by relevance/recency rather than brand prominence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience growth,” or “multi-channel communications” here; those are already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies.
- Don’t repeat analytics or automation terms already listed under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** or **Automation & Workflow Systems**.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” It would be stronger if it emphasized technical depth and execution-oriented capabilities rather than repeating broad analytics terms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to focus on platforms + applied methods: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Tag Manager • SEO analysis • Experimentation”
- Replace vague nouns like “Dashboarding” with a more specific capability such as “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards.”
- Use consistent technical phrasing: swap “A/B testing” for “Experimentation” if you want a more senior, strategic tone.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to outcomes in recent roles instead of listing them twice (e.g., analytics infrastructure, reporting, optimization).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one version.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid over-repeating them across sections.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles on workflows, video, and digital operations. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and support daily execution across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add specific outputs/results where possible: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, engagement growth, or production volume.
- Tighten the leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize cross-channel publishing workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo entries; keep this version focused on building the function, not later operational leadership.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the next role; distinguish this as launch/early production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outputs, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope + standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; produced digital and multimedia content to extend project visibility and member engagement.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and lead with ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to” with stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “supported.”
- If possible, add one concrete outcome: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Don’t overemphasize general digital content production; later roles already cover web, video, and multimedia leadership in more depth.
- Avoid repeating “policy work” and “multimedia production” language used elsewhere unless tied to a distinct achievement here.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production tools and avoid repeating broader multimedia themes already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename or sharpen scope: “Multimedia Production Tools” is clearer than “Multimedia & Creative Tools.”
- Separate tools from capabilities; keep this line software-focused and move workflow terms only if they are true technical proficiencies.
- Suggested rewrite: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio production • Podcast recording, editing & production”
- If accurate, add stronger specificity instead of generic workflows, e.g. “PTZ camera control,” “live switching,” or “audio mixing,” which better signal hands-on technical depth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Topline Skills: “Livestreaming • Studio operations • Hybrid and virtual event production.”
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older work experience; keep it only if you want to preserve multimedia breadth.
